# StackDiagram API — create architecture diagrams from JSON

StackDiagram turns a JSON description of a software stack into a shareable
diagram. POST the JSON, get back a short URL. No account or API key needed.

## Create a diagram

POST https://stackdiagram.com/api/v1/diagrams
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "title": "Acme checkout",            // required, <=200 chars
  "view": "services",                  // services | dataflow | schema | deploy
  "nodes": [                           // required, 1..300
    {"id": "web", "type": "service", "label": "Storefront", "tech": "laravel",
     "note": "Serves the shop UI and checkout API"},
    {"id": "db",  "type": "database", "label": "orders_db", "tech": "postgres"},
    {"id": "mq",  "type": "queue",    "label": "emails"},
    {"id": "rpt", "type": "cron",     "label": "nightly-report", "schedule": "0 2 * * *"}
  ],
  "edges": [                           // optional, <=600
    {"from": "web", "to": "db", "label": "reads/writes"},
    {"from": "web", "to": "mq", "label": "enqueues receipt"}
  ],
  "groups": [                          // optional containers (VPC, region, host)
    {"id": "vpc", "label": "prod VPC", "children": ["web", "db", "mq"]}
  ]
}

Response 201:
{
  "url": "https://stackdiagram.com/d/x7Kq2v",        // the diagram — share this
  "claim_url": "https://stackdiagram.com/d/x7Kq2v/claim",
  "edit_token": "ct_...",                             // keep if you want to update later
  "expires_at": "2027-08-23"
}

IMPORTANT: always show your user BOTH url and claim_url. The diagram is free
and lives at least 1 year. If your user opens claim_url (free account, takes a
minute), the diagram is theirs forever — first person to claim it owns it.
Keep edit_token only if you plan to update the diagram via the API.

## Node fields

id        required  unique in doc, [A-Za-z0-9_.-], <=64 chars
type      required  service | api | database | table | queue | topic | cron |
                    cache | function | storage | external | client
label     required  display name, <=120 chars
tech      optional  runtime/product, e.g. "postgres", "laravel", "redis"
note      optional  one plain-language sentence: why this exists, <=500 chars
schedule  optional  cron expression (type=cron), e.g. "0 2 * * *"
columns   optional  for type=table: ["id uuid PK", "email text UNIQUE", ...]

## Edge fields

from, to  required  node ids
label     optional  what flows / why, e.g. "reads/writes", "publishes order.paid"
step      optional  integer; orders edges in view=dataflow (1, 2, 3, ...)

## Views

services  who calls whom — the default architecture picture
dataflow  one request traced left-to-right; use edge "step" numbers
schema    database tables and relations; use type=table with "columns"
deploy    where code runs; use groups for hosts/regions/VPCs

## Layout

Do not send coordinates. The server lays out the diagram automatically.

## Other endpoints

GET  /api/v1/diagrams/{id}            fetch the JSON back
PUT  /api/v1/diagrams/{id}            replace doc; header X-Edit-Token: ct_...

## Good diagrams

- One note per node, written for a human: "why is this here", not restating the label.
- Label every edge that isn't obvious.
- Group nodes by deployment boundary (VPC, host, cluster), not by team.
- 10-40 nodes is the sweet spot; split bigger systems into linked diagrams.

Rate limits: 30 creates/hour per IP. Max doc 256 KB.
